x: Our first counter was Steve Charlton who finished 4th, and we were pleased to see Les. Stokell turning out for us once again, and he ran well in being 7th, as did C.
Bromley of the Police was first man home just in front of Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown. Les. Stokell, now back down South once again, came next with Ted Stimpson, R.
At the end of the first lap Vern Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt were running stride for stride in the lead followed by Les Stokell and Jack Brown.

Stone had increased his lead when they came round again and although Len Herbert was still with Butler and Wheeler of Surrey, with Les Stokell close behind the rest of our chaps had fallen back and we were hoping for a usual last lap Belgrave effort.
On the day Len Herbert and Les Stokell were non-starters, and Bill Lucas was first home of our members competing and this certainly seems to be a race in which our lads are not inclined to shine.

Les Stokell who finished in tenth place was one of these and Jack Brown also came in minus his shoes. Vern Blowfield after making a fast start had a bad time and fell right back but came through again later on to finish in the first 100.
Les Stokell ran his usual determined kind of race while Jack Brown seemed content to take matters easy in front of Archie Bedford, Steve Charlton and Jack Bragginton.
Les Stokell was our next man over the long and crucial stage from Hanacross to Hickstead and our best time for this leg was Tom Carter's 30.26 in 1937, while Vern Blowfield did 30.40 in 1948.

Les Stokell won the individual race with Syd Ring third and Bert Footer fourth. Bert was running for our “ B ” team, otherwise we should have scored a hollow win in the team race but even so we still came out winners and Syd Ring also took 2nd prize in the individual handicap race.
On Whit-Monday our team scored a good win over Portsmouth A.C. and Thames Valley H. in the team race. Les Stokell ran well to once again finish 2nd to A.

Arthur Bruce was second in the 880 yards and Stan Davies had to run a quarter in order to gain a point for third place. Our bright "spot" was the 1 mile win of Bill Lucas in 4 min. 29 secs. and that of Les. Stokell in the 2 miles run in 9 min. 54.8 secs.
Held at Swindon on August 5th over a 15-mile course. Les.

Len Herbert and Jack Braughton, both International runners, came in together for fourth place, and then came Les Stokell ninth, with John Bromley, running his first race for us since he became qualified, in tenth position, and we had the spectacle of four Belgraves fighting for the honour to be our…

Les Stokell and John Bromley were also present as reserves for Surrey and it is a pity that this county has now dropped down the list and one thinks of the days of Bert Footer and Arthur Penny, who used to lead Surrey to victory in pre-war years.
Among these were Vern Blowfield and Les Stokell, while Archie Bedford also stated his intention to do only one lap but then evidently changed his mind and ran well to finish in 4th position.
In the straight running events we did well, with Jack Brown winning the half-mile, Reg Bolam taking the 1 mile and Bill Lucas the 3 miles, with Les Stokell in second place.

In the 100 yards " Ginger " Holtum finished second, with Bob Taylor in a similar position in the 880 yards. Ray Tooby was second in the 1 mile and Les Stokell was runner-up to Alec Olney in the 2 miles run.

It was only through Bill " pepping " up the pace with a lap to go that the field broke up and this enabled Walker to use his stronger finishing powers to good advantage. In the 3 miles run we had Les Stokell and Archie Bedford, and they finished fourth and fifth, to score some useful points.
A feature of the above was the promise shewn by I. Badiali in the 440 yards, the strong running of Les Stokell in the mile, and Denis Merrett's fine hurdling.
It speaks well for Bill's presence of mind that he was able to make up the lost ground and our other two scoring men were Les Stokell and Len Adams.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yards, with Jim Heathfield second, and Dicky Bartlett was second in the 220, while Bill Lucas was first home in the 2 miles run, with Les Stokell second.

On the fifth stage Blackheath kept their lead and Les Stokell ran a dogged race to hang on to 2nd place and here again his time compared well with previous times recorded by our men, although nearly a minute slower than Charlie Smart's record breaking run for this " leg " last April.

Congratulations to Les Stokell and Mrs. Stokell on the birth of a daughter and if we get many more female additions to the club strength, we shall have to consider starting a ladies' section, shades of Footer!

The Shot Putt handicap was won by Les Stokell who is now taking up field events, he has ideas about becoming a decathion performer, and he certainly did well to take first place in the handicap with Frank Kemp second and a new member in R.

Our other men to finish, with nine to compete and six to score, were Les Stokell 64th, Albert Frost 95th, and finally Dick Tobin 132nd. Les Stokell
42 · Les Stokell · Mar 50

The Southern Champs the following month at Eastbourne at which the Club usually made a strong showing resulted in another 4th place behind T.V.H., Aylesford and Blackheath, our first man home being Les Stokell with a good performance by evergreen Ted Stimpson in 21st place.

Our positions were as follows:- 3 V.S.Blowfield 56:46; 4 E.S.Stimpson 57:24; 7 L.W.Herbert 57:50; 10 F.J.Abberton 58:05; 15 T.P.Clinton 58:20; 36 C.T.Carter 60:01; 38 C.L.Stokell 60:05; 65 R.W.Tobin 61:37; 84 S.R.Eales 62:25; 90 A.E.Frost 62:50; 106 A.F.Mitchell 63:28; 132 G.M.Pearson 64:15.
The Seniors, led home by Les Stokell were 8th; the Juniors with Charlie Walker in 40th place were 21st and the Youths with Don Maclean in 18th place were 7th.
Les Stokell passed away at Sidmouth in Devon on 20 January 2001 in his 82nd year. He was an active club member in the early post-war years, having joined the Club at the age of 27 in 1946.
